Relabel and direct MAIN as a positive find (proud or curious delivery on 'found'), or the E2 result cannot be read as hook type alone.

FACTS says the analyser's judge verdicts are not measured, and the labeller is a separate frame-only coach (confidence 0.6). Either add 'run the judge on IMG_2649 and confirm CONTINUE' to the pre-recording slot list, or the TRIAL line is unsupported.

Change it to 'beat your own best marks, not the topper's' (and 'MY BEST MARKS'). Otherwise the line viewers are meant to forward teaches the wrong rule.

FACTS gives four causes: the 0.2 s tracker jump (0.8 s rule), the 11° rep (under-30° limit), and the half reps 1 and 14 cut by the clip start and end (removal method not stated). Comment trigger mismatch. The reel explains the analyser (17 joints, knee wave, best-set baseline, judge), but JARVIS delivers `form-labeller`, a frame-only coach with no pose data or baseline. Label it accurately on screen and in the caption (for example 'my AI form-coach skill'), or ship the analyser. Keep the CTA blocked until item 5 is confirmed.

Beats 6 and 7 are two E beats in a row. Beat 7's rule is a good 'So always…' action, but consider folding it into the end of beat 6, or tagging beat 7 as H (a direct-to-viewer rule), to keep the emotion-hook rhythm. Beat 7 is also listed as droppable, so the story must still read without it, which it does.

Beat 6 'Now my AI says can't see' states the guardrail message in present tense. FACTS only measures that frames are thrown out, not that a can't-see string is printed. Keep pre-recording item 4 as a hard gate, and keep `[CAN'T-SEE STRING]` as a slot until real output exists.

Beat 9 'It compares every rep with my own best set' and the judge box describe a judge that FACTS marks as still being built. Gate recording on the judge actually running against the baseline (item 4), not only on the slots being filled.

Beat 5 on-screen 'ACTUAL REPS 11' is the labeller's count (cross-checked by the clean count). Consider 'COACH COUNT 11' or keep the label, but fix the source key: the Labels source is marked as a slot even though the 11-rep verdict is already in FACTS.

Process: the draft is unscored. It needs the Fable judge and the frozen 16-persona panel at 7.5 or above before it reaches the creator, and the E2 entry belongs in production/EXPERIMENTS.md before recording.

personas.why: The broken trace is the bit I'd send to my support team: you can see exactly when the system should stop trusting its input.
I stayed to see 14 reconcile to 11. When the green line turns out to be his personal best, I understand the comparison but not why the difference warrants STOP.
I wanted to see what he did wrong. I can follow the knee wave, but now I'm watching a rep counter for a different set.
The red gap gets me past three seconds. The fault freeze gives me my answer, and 'How my AI reads a set' sounds like the start of a tutorial I didn't come for.
Watching the dots lose the leg makes 'I don't know' a memorable lesson. When the counter comes back, I feel I've already seen the part I'd tell someone about.
I could show a project friend how a knee angle becomes a counter, where it fails, and what the fix looks like. I'd comment JARVIS to try it on a clip.
The 14-versus-11 check and the personal baseline both interest me. By the report cards I understand the benchmark; I'm still waiting for the actual decision.
Checking the count earns some trust. A match against one chosen best set doesn't tell me how often the judge wrongly calls STOP, which is the claim I care about.
I'd stay to see the first clip run through the finished diagram. The hidden-leg example is easier to share with a colleague than the crowded diagram itself.
The useful idea for my team is letting the system decline a call. Nearly half a minute in, we're only now asking the question the opening promised to answer.
The stamp gets my attention and the quiet 'I did 11' wins it back. I'd watch for the opening-frame callback, but 'access the skill' gives me little reason to comment.
I remember the ghost and the surprise of 14 versus 11. With an angle, a broken trace and rejected-frame counts on screen, I lose the story of the lifter.
The 0.2-second jump followed by the duration filter is a fix I can inspect, not just a polished demo. I'd try the skill to see what it rejects on my footage.
I'd save the occlusion sequence: missing data stays missing on screen. I watch through the verdict to see its evidence, though validating rep counts doesn't validate form judgments.
I wait for the same-point best-versus-bad freeze so I can judge the fault myself. That's useful to discuss with a client; a gap from someone's best alone isn't a reason I'd stop them.
I get 'it said 14, he did 11' instantly. Once I'm reading how many frames got thrown out, I'd rather see the bad rep again.

top_fixes: Keep STOP on frame one, but label the green ghost MY BEST and name the visible fault within three seconds. Use '1 FLAGGED' only if exactly one set was flagged; finding one STOP doesn't establish that it was the only one.

Keep the 14-versus-11 reveal and pay it off before leaving the wave: show which detections were removed and the corrected 11. Then show the hidden leg as a separate reason to withhold a reading. Move the frame totals to the caption.

Spend the school-analogy seconds on the matched best/bad freeze. Let viewers see the specific fault that drove this call; describe what the analyser flagged rather than implying it knows what injury the rep would have caused.
Make the comment offer concrete. Show one example of what a viewer gets back from their own clip, and state what they need to run the shared skill before asking for JARVIS.
